title: Coherent modules on a closed subscheme are the coherent modules annihilated by its ideal; the same for coherent formal modules
statement: Let $i:Z\to X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] of locally Noetherian schemes [pqf-def-locnoeth] and $\mathcal J\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ its quasi-coherent ideal sheaf [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. (1) The functor $i_*$ (pushforward of modules [def-pc-module-pullback]) induces an equivalence between the category of coherent $\mathcal O_Z$-modules [pqf-def-coherent] and the full subcategory of the coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules $\mathcal F$ with $\mathcal J\mathcal F=0$; moreover $\operatorname{Supp}(i_*\mathcal G)=i(\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal G)$ [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base]. (2) Consequently, if $X$ is Noetherian and $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ is a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals, with $\mathcal I\mathcal O_Z\subseteq\mathcal O_Z$ the image of $i^*\mathcal I\to\mathcal O_Z$ [def-nagata-extended-ideal], then $(\mathcal G_n)\mapsto(i_*\mathcal G_n)$ is an equivalence from $\mathit{Coh}(Z,\mathcal I\mathcal O_Z)$ onto the full subcategory of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ of the objects supported on $Z$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module], and $i_*(\mathcal G^\wedge)\cong(i_*\mathcal G)^\wedge$ naturally in the coherent $\mathcal O_Z$-module $\mathcal G$ (as $i_*(\mathcal G/(\mathcal I\mathcal O_Z)^n\mathcal G)=i_*\mathcal G/\mathcal I^n i_*\mathcal G$).

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 087T (lemma-i-star-equivalence) for (1); (2) is the use of 087T 'without further mention' in the proofs of Lemma 088A (lemma-existence-tricky), Proposition 088C (proposition-existence-proper) and Theorem 088E (theorem-grothendieck-existence)

proof.text: (Conventions; $Z$ Noetherian.) For a quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal K$ and an $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$, $\mathcal K\mathcal F$ is the subsheaf generated by the local products $as$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] (0); so $\mathcal K\mathcal F=0$ iff $as=0$ for every open $V$, $a\in\mathcal K(V)$, $s\in\mathcal F(V)$, which is the meaning of '$\mathcal I\mathcal F=0$' in [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-pushforward-annihilated]. In (2), $X$ is Noetherian (locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] with quasi-compact underlying space). Then so is $Z$: for an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $X$ with $R$ Noetherian, $i^{-1}(U)\cong\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)$ for an ideal $I$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], and $R/I$ is Noetherian, so the affine opens $i^{-1}(U_k)$ for an affine Noetherian cover $(U_k)$ of $X$ cover $Z$; and $Z$ is homeomorphic to the closed subset $i(Z)$ of the quasi-compact space $X$, hence quasi-compact.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Section 0EHN (section-coherent-formal) for the notation; Noetherian closed subschemes: Morphisms, Lemma 01T6 (morphisms-lemma-finite-type-noetherian) and Lemma 01QO (morphisms-lemma-closed-immersion), literature/stacks-project/morphisms.tex

proof.text: ($i_*$ maps $\mathit{Coh}(\mathcal O_Z)$ into the coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules killed by $\mathcal J$.) Let $\mathcal G$ be a coherent $\mathcal O_Z$-module. A closed immersion is finite [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite] and $X$ is locally Noetherian, so $i_*\mathcal G$ is coherent [lem-weil-pbc-finite-pushforward-coherent]. As $Z$ is locally Noetherian, $\mathcal G$ is quasi-coherent (of finite type) [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth], so $\mathcal J(i_*\mathcal G)=0$ [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-pushforward-annihilated] (1). Hence $i_*$ restricts to a functor from $\mathit{Coh}(\mathcal O_Z)$ to the full subcategory $\mathit{Coh}_{\mathcal J}(\mathcal O_X)$ of the coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules $\mathcal F$ with $\mathcal J\mathcal F=0$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 087T (lemma-i-star-equivalence), statement (that i_* lands in the coherent modules annihilated by I is left implicit there); Lemma 01Y6 (lemma-finite-pushforward-coherent); Morphisms, Lemma 035C (morphisms-lemma-closed-immersion-finite) and Lemma 01QY (morphisms-lemma-i-star-equivalence)

proof.text: (Fully faithful.) By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-pushforward-fully-faithful], $\varphi\mapsto i_*\varphi$ is a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_Z}(\mathcal G,\mathcal G')\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(i_*\mathcal G,i_*\mathcal G')$ for all $\mathcal O_Z$-modules, in particular for coherent ones; since both $\mathit{Coh}(\mathcal O_Z)$ and $\mathit{Coh}_{\mathcal J}(\mathcal O_X)$ are full subcategories of the module categories, the functor of step 2 is fully faithful. In particular it reflects isomorphisms, and an $\mathcal O_Z$-module $\mathcal H$ with $i_*\mathcal H=0$ is $0$ (every open of $Z$ is $i^{-1}(V)$ for an open $V\subseteq X$, $i$ being a homeomorphism onto a subspace, and $\mathcal H(i^{-1}V)=(i_*\mathcal H)(V)$).

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 087T: 'The functor is fully faithful by Morphisms, Lemma 01QY', which rests on Modules, Lemma 08KS (modules-lemma-i-star-equivalence)

proof.text: (Essentially surjective.) Let $\mathcal F$ be a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module with $\mathcal J\mathcal F=0$. It is quasi-coherent of finite type [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth], so by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-pushforward-annihilated] (2) $i^*\mathcal F$ is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Z$-module of finite type and the unit $\eta_{\mathcal F}:\mathcal F\to i_*i^*\mathcal F$ is an isomorphism. As $Z$ is locally Noetherian, $i^*\mathcal F$ is coherent [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]. So $\mathcal F\cong i_*\mathcal G$ with $\mathcal G=i^*\mathcal F$ coherent. (Stacks writes $\mathcal F=i_*\mathcal G$ with $\mathcal G$ quasi-coherent and gets finite type from Modules Lemma 01C4; here finite type of $\mathcal G=i^*\mathcal F$ comes from the pullback of a finite type module, Modules Lemma 01B6, as recorded in the cited node.) A fully faithful, essentially surjective functor is an equivalence of categories; with steps 2 and 3 this proves the equivalence in (1).

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 087T (essential surjectivity), with Lemma 01XZ (lemma-coherent-Noetherian)

proof.text: (Support.) Let $\mathcal G$ be an $\mathcal O_Z$-module and $x\in X$; supports are as in [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base] (2). If $x\notin i(Z)$ then $(i_*\mathcal G)_x=0$ [lem-weil-pbc-closed-pushforward-stalks] (1), so $x\notin\operatorname{Supp}(i_*\mathcal G)$. If $x=i(z)$ ($z$ unique, $i$ being injective) then $(i_*\mathcal G)_x\cong\mathcal G_z$ [lem-weil-pbc-closed-pushforward-stalks] (2), so $x\in\operatorname{Supp}(i_*\mathcal G)$ iff $z\in\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal G$. Hence $\operatorname{Supp}(i_*\mathcal G)=i(\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal G)$.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma 00AE (sheaves-lemma-stalks-closed-pushforward); the support formula is not stated in Stacks' Lemma 087T (written out by the agent)

proof.text: (The ideal $\mathcal I\mathcal O_Z$ and the quotients.) In the situation of (2), $\mathcal I\mathcal O_Z$ [def-nagata-extended-ideal] is a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals of the Noetherian scheme $Z$ (step 1) [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-pushforward-ideal-powers] (1), so $\mathit{Coh}(Z,\mathcal I\mathcal O_Z)$ is defined [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] (1). For a coherent (hence quasi-coherent, [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]) $\mathcal O_Z$-module $\mathcal G$ and $n\ge1$, $i_*((\mathcal I\mathcal O_Z)^n\mathcal G)=\mathcal I^n(i_*\mathcal G)$, and $i_*$ of the quotient map induces an isomorphism $\rho^n_{\mathcal G}:i_*\mathcal G/\mathcal I^n i_*\mathcal G\to i_*(\mathcal G/(\mathcal I\mathcal O_Z)^n\mathcal G)$, natural in $\mathcal G$ and compatible with the quotient maps between levels [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-pushforward-ideal-powers] (2), (3).

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 088A (lemma-existence-tricky), lines 6961-6968 (Coh(X_e, I_e) identified with the objects of Coh(X, I) annihilated by K^e, 'without further mention')

proof.text: (The functor on systems.) Let $(\mathcal G_n)$ be an object of $\mathit{Coh}(Z,\mathcal I\mathcal O_Z)$ with transition maps $t_n$, and put $\mathcal F_n=i_*\mathcal G_n$ with transition maps $i_*t_n$. Each $\mathcal F_n$ is coherent with $\mathcal J\mathcal F_n=0$ (step 2). $\mathcal I^n\mathcal F_n=i_*((\mathcal I\mathcal O_Z)^n\mathcal G_n)=i_*0=0$ (step 6). The map $\mathcal F_{n+1}/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F_{n+1}\to\mathcal F_n$ induced by $i_*t_n$ equals $i_*(\bar t_n)\circ\rho^n_{\mathcal G_{n+1}}$, where $\bar t_n:\mathcal G_{n+1}/(\mathcal I\mathcal O_Z)^n\mathcal G_{n+1}\to\mathcal G_n$ is the isomorphism induced by $t_n$ (both composites with the quotient map of $\mathcal F_{n+1}$ are $i_*t_n$, and the quotient map is an epimorphism [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] (0)); so it is an isomorphism. Hence $(\mathcal F_n)$ is an object of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ annihilated by $\mathcal J$, i.e. supported on $Z$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] (3); a morphism $(\beta_n)$ goes to $(i_*\beta_n)$, which commutes with the transition maps by functoriality. This is the functor $(\mathcal G_n)\mapsto(i_*\mathcal G_n)$ of (2).

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 088A, lines 6961-6968, and proof of Theorem 088E, lines 7658-7663 ('supported on Z'); written out by the agent

proof.text: (Fully faithful on systems.) Let $(\mathcal G_n),(\mathcal G'_n)$ be objects of $\mathit{Coh}(Z,\mathcal I\mathcal O_Z)$ and $(\alpha_n):(i_*\mathcal G_n)\to(i_*\mathcal G'_n)$ a morphism of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$. By step 3 there are unique $\beta_n:\mathcal G_n\to\mathcal G'_n$ with $i_*\beta_n=\alpha_n$, and $i_*(t'_n\beta_{n+1})=i_*(t'_n)\alpha_{n+1}=\alpha_n i_*(t_n)=i_*(\beta_nt_n)$ gives $t'_n\beta_{n+1}=\beta_nt_n$ by faithfulness. So $(\beta_n)\mapsto(i_*\beta_n)$ is bijective on morphisms.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Section 0EHN (morphisms of Coh(X, I) componentwise) and Lemma 087T; written out by the agent

proof.text: (Essentially surjective onto the systems supported on $Z$.) Let $(\mathcal F_n)$ be an object of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ with $\mathcal J\mathcal F_n=0$ for all $n$, transition maps $s_n$. By step 4 choose coherent $\mathcal O_Z$-modules $\mathcal G_n$ and isomorphisms $\varphi_n:i_*\mathcal G_n\to\mathcal F_n$; by step 3 there are unique $t_n:\mathcal G_{n+1}\to\mathcal G_n$ with $i_*t_n=\varphi_n^{-1}s_n\varphi_{n+1}$. As $\varphi_n$ is $\mathcal O_X$-linear, $\varphi_n(\mathcal I^ni_*\mathcal G_n)=\mathcal I^n\mathcal F_n=0$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] (0), so $i_*((\mathcal I\mathcal O_Z)^n\mathcal G_n)=\mathcal I^ni_*\mathcal G_n=0$ (step 6) and $(\mathcal I\mathcal O_Z)^n\mathcal G_n=0$ (step 3). The map $\bar t_n:\mathcal G_{n+1}/(\mathcal I\mathcal O_Z)^n\mathcal G_{n+1}\to\mathcal G_n$ induced by $t_n$ satisfies $i_*(\bar t_n)\circ\rho^n_{\mathcal G_{n+1}}=\varphi_n^{-1}\circ\bar s_n\circ\bar\varphi_{n+1}$, with $\bar s_n$ the isomorphism induced by $s_n$ and $\bar\varphi_{n+1}$ the isomorphism induced by $\varphi_{n+1}$ on the quotients by $\mathcal I^n$; so $i_*(\bar t_n)$ is an isomorphism and so is $\bar t_n$ (step 3). Thus $(\mathcal G_n)$ is an object of $\mathit{Coh}(Z,\mathcal I\mathcal O_Z)$ and $(\varphi_n):(i_*\mathcal G_n)\to(\mathcal F_n)$ is an isomorphism of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$. With steps 7 and 8, $(\mathcal G_n)\mapsto(i_*\mathcal G_n)$ is an equivalence onto the full subcategory of objects supported on $Z$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 088A, lines 6961-6968; written out by the agent

proof.text: (Completion.) For a coherent $\mathcal O_Z$-module $\mathcal G$, $\mathcal G^\wedge=(\mathcal G/(\mathcal I\mathcal O_Z)^n\mathcal G)_n$ and $(i_*\mathcal G)^\wedge=(i_*\mathcal G/\mathcal I^ni_*\mathcal G)_n$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] (2), with the canonical surjections as transition maps ($i_*\mathcal G$ is coherent by step 2). The isomorphisms $\rho^n_{\mathcal G}$ of step 6 are compatible with the transition maps and natural in $\mathcal G$, so $(\rho^n_{\mathcal G})_n:(i_*\mathcal G)^\wedge\to i_*(\mathcal G^\wedge)$ is an isomorphism of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$, natural in $\mathcal G$.
